t:
(a) 
Requirement of Authorizing Legislation.—Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no appropriation shall be made under any law to the Department of Commerce for expenses to carry out the purposes of this Act unless previously and specifically authorized by law.
 
    (b) 
Authorization.—There are authorized to be appropriated to the Department of Commerce to carry out the purposes of this Act—

        (1) 
$8,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 1980 and 1981, of which $1,250,000 shall be available for each such fiscal year only for purposes of carrying out foreign availability assessments pursuant to section 5(f)(5), and
 
        (2) 
such additional amounts, for each such fiscal year, as may be necessary for increases in salary, pay, retirement, other employee benefits authorized by law, and other nondiscretionary costs.

fable.w: This section only requires prior authorizing legislation and authorizes appropriations to the Department of Commerce. The tempting reading is that the authorization requirement or the 'foreign availability assessments' imply some consultative process, but the only actors are Congress and a federal department, both inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Department of Commerce to carry out the purposes of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section solely concerns the authorization of federal appropriations for the Department of Commerce. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The text describes internal budgetary authority rather than public participation.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Department of Commerce to carry out the purposes of this Act— (1) $8,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 1980 and 1981

opus.w: This section only requires authorizing legislation before money is appropriated and authorizes funding for the Department of Commerce, including money set aside for foreign availability assessments. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of assessments is a funding allocation, not a process that brings outsiders into a federal decision.

But this section only sets aside money for those assessments. It doesn't require consulting, holding hearings with, or getting comments from anyone outside the federal government. The rest is a rule requiring authorizing legislation before money is appropriated, plus dollar amounts. No actor outside the federal government appears anywhere.

The decision-making process described involves the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Army, who are federal officials, and an ad hoc committee appointed by the Research and Development Board (a federal body). qwen_chat.s: That there is hereby authorized to be appropriated not to exceed $11,000,000 for the acquisition of land and for the construction thereon of a research laboratory for the Quartermaster Corps, United States Army, at a location to be selected by the Secretary of Defense, and for such utilities and appurtenances thereto as, in the judgment of the Secretary of the Army, may be necessary in connection therewith. The site shall be chosen on the basis of recommendations of an impartial ad hoc committee of experts to be appointed by the Research and Development Board.
